newsitem.title: EGYPT: Syria says Israel is the one running away from peace.
newsitem.headline: Syria says Israel is the one running away from peace.

text.p: Syrian Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara said on Saturday that Israel was running away from peace and that Syria was willing to resume peace talks as long as they started where the previous round left off.

Talks between Syria and Israel broke off last March when a Labour government was still in power in the Jewish state. Syria says that government, which lost to Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party in elections last May, agreed to withdraw from the Golan, captured from Syria in the 1967 Middle East war.
"There is no Syrian obstinacy as Netanyahu claims and Syria is not distancing itself from the peace process or its elements as some enemy media are trying to say," Shara told reporters.

"The Israeli government is the one running away from peace and not the Syrian leadership. Syria is ready to resume negotiations tomorrow if Israel abides by what was reached during the previous stage," he added.
Shara was speaking in Cairo after he and Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam discussed the latest developments in the Middle East peace process with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
The visit coincides with one to Washington by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who had talks with U.S. President Bill Clinton on how to revive Syrian-Israeli peace talks.

"The Syrian position is clear. We are ready to resume peace talks from the point at which they stopped and with the commitments that were reached during the past years of negotiations. It is not logical to return to square one but we must follow on from what was reached," Shara said.
In Washington on Friday Netanyahu said: "Obviously we will take note of what took place in the talks between Syrian negotiators and the previous (Israeli) government."
But he added: "We cannot be bound by conversations or by ideas or by speculations and suggestions and hypotheses. We can only honour signed agreements."

The Syrian officials, whose last visit to Cairo was less than a month ago, gave Mubarak a message from President Hafez al-Assad. Shara said: "It concerned the peace process and the bases for this peace process."

"If any government backs away from the commitments during the previous negotiations conducted with the previous government this is in fact a lack of respect to its own government and it is lack of respect to its country," Shara said.

Syria has condemned Netanyahu for refusing to trade occupied Arab land for peace and has launched an Arab campaign to put pressure on the current Israeli government to change its attitude towards peace with Arabs.
Khaddam and Shara have toured many Arab states during the last two weeks to rally support for Damascus's conditions for resuming talks with Israel.
